reference_line.info: Median of real cases, applied to Wisconsin: the median of the 76 repeal places changed by -0.12 permits per 1,000 existing homes per year against its comparison places. Applied to Wisconsin's 2,684,793 homes outside places already at the benchmark, the median is below zero, so the line sits at 0, the same as the central case (a repeal is not modelled as reducing permits).
reference_line.label: Median of real cases

scenarios.info: Like the 76 US places that removed parking minimums: in the one to three years after, their permit rates did not rise measurably compared with similar places that kept them.
scenarios.label: No measurable change

scenarios.info: If the true average effect is at the top of what the evidence allows (95 times in 100, the real average would be lower): 1.49 more permits per 1,000 existing homes per year, everywhere except places that already have no parking minimums for housing.
scenarios.label: High end of the evidence

scenarios.info: The measured average of the 76 repeal places against similar places: -1.14 permits per 1,000 existing homes per year. It is pulled down mostly by San Francisco and Minneapolis, whose permits fell after repeal while their metro neighbours' did not; the typical repeal place changed by about 0. Shown without a floor at zero.
scenarios.label: Low end of the evidence
